rationale: Both are short, data-driven and correct. A keeps each animal's name and comment together in one struct slice, which is cohesive and easy to extend. Its verse logic reads straightforwardly: an opening line, an optional comment, the chain of 'swallowed X to catch Y' lines, then the refrain for every verse but the last. B's parallel animals and comments slices are less cohesive. B also reuses comments[0] as both the fly verse's comment and the shared refrain, which needs the extra 'v > 1 && v < len(animals)' condition to avoid a duplicate. That is clever but makes the control flow harder to follow. B is better on two smaller points: it uses len(animals) instead of a hard-coded 8, and its catcher-suffix trick avoids A's repeated spider sentence. Overall A's structure is clearer.
